original.target_description: Study 1: point-biserial correlation between conception risk and binary intention to vote for Barack Obama (versus all other options), among eligible white female Michigan State University students aged 18–22. PDF page 3 (printed page 396).

n.sample_role: Analytic participants: white women aged 18–22 in Study 1; section 2.1.1 explicitly identifies observations included in the analyses below.
n.exclusions: Data culled to white US citizens without chronic health problems, with normal-length menstrual cycles, not pregnant, willing to state voting preference, and not using hormonal contraceptives. Exclusion counts are not printed.
n.location: Printed p. 396 (third article page), section 2.1.1 Research subjects; section 2.2 Results
n.quote: described below include observations from 62 white women

es.location: Printed p. 396 (third article page), section 2.2 Results

replication.target_description: Edlund direct replication final report: pooled Stage Two final sample, correlation between conception risk and binary preference for Obama over Trump, with other candidate/not voting coded as Trump. Final pooled test selected; Stage One is separately reported.

n.sample_role: Final pooled eligible participant sample for Stage Two correlation
n.exclusions: Eligibility screening is mentioned but criteria and exclusion counts are not documented in the final report. Stage One had 226 eligible participants; Stage Two added 319.

n.quote: I collected data from 319 eligible participants (resulting in a final sample of 545).

notes:
Original title and authors verified against supplied reference. Replication OSF node title and final report identify the supplied study and Edlund team; dyn6j is the final-report DOCX, not a node. Original locator p. 3 identifies Study 1 correlation. Replication reports r, retained as printed despite requested phi; no conversion performed. Stage One reports r(226)= -.086, p=.195; final pooled Stage Two selected for replication values. Replication uses Obama versus Trump, a documented adaptation of the original Obama versus McCain question. No further replication locator was supplied. Final report provides no fixed page numbering; section and paragraph cited.
Completion source review (n_o): Study 1 methods explicitly state that the analyses below include observations from 62 white women. The p. 3 locator identifies this study and its point-biserial correlation. Final analytic participant count printed directly; no sum or df inference. Eligibility restrictions recorded in checkpoint exclusions.
Completion source review (es_value_o): On the located third article page, Study 1 Results explicitly identify a point-biserial correlation of conception risk with voting preference. Retained printed r and precision, with same-test p=.03; no conversion.
